text: Hi, how's it going? I'm a big coffee lover, so I guess I'll start there. I can't really start my day without a cup of coffee, and this morning was no different. I had one before I came to take this test, and I'm already looking forward to another one once it's over. I work in IT, and my days are pretty busy. I live in an apartment, and I'm pretty much a homebody. In my free time, I like listening to music, playing computer games, and reading. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell: coffee, music, and my computer. I'm happy to be here, and I hope I do well today!

Well, I live in an apartment in a small city by the sea. It isn't fancy, but it's comfortable. We have three bedrooms. One is the master bedroom, one is a guest room, and the third is my own little room, with my computer. Besides that, there's a living room, a kitchen, and two bathrooms. But my favorite spot is the balcony. We put a small table and two chairs there, and I call it my "coffee corner". On a nice morning, I sit there with a hot coffee and watch the sun come up over the sea. You can't beat that.

Weekdays are a blur for me. I wake up around 6, make a big cup of coffee, and grab a quick bite. Then I'm out the door by 7:30. When I get back, I'm usually wiped out. I eat dinner with my family, and if I still have energy left, I play a game or read for a bit. Then it's lights out by 11. Weekends are a whole different story. I sleep in until 8, which feels like a luxury! Then I grind some fresh coffee beans, and the whole house smells amazing. After brunch, I might go to the market with a friend or just hang around the house. In the evening, I like to cook something simple, like pasta, and watch a movie. I'm not a "go out" kind of guy. I'm happiest at home, to be honest.

I grew up in an old house with a yard. The thing I remember best is the persimmon tree in the yard. Every fall, it was full of orange fruit, and my friends and I would pick them with a long stick. I was the smallest kid, so I always got the leftovers! The house itself wasn't big, and we all slept in one room. In the winter, the floor was warm, but the air was freezing. We'd all pile onto one blanket. It was cozy, but crowded. Now, it's a whole new world. My apartment is warm in every room, and I even have a little space to myself. It's a lot more convenient. The thing is, I miss the persimmon tree. Nobody gives you free fruit in an apartment! I guess you can't have everything.

I'm a big fan of sci-fi and thriller movies. I love it when a movie makes me think, or when there's a big twist at the end. I mean, I'm the kind of guy who stays in his seat during the credits, trying to figure out what just happened. I'm into sci-fi because it shows me things I can't see in real life, like space travel, robots, and the future. Maybe that's because I work in IT. Thrillers keep me on the edge of my seat. My friend likes romance and comedies, so we take turns picking. I'll watch hers, and she'll watch mine, and we usually end up happy. For me, a movie is the best way to escape for two hours.

The last time I went to the movies was last Saturday, with a friend. We went to a theater in town. Before the movie, we had dinner at a little noodle place nearby. We almost missed the show, because the food took forever! We ran into the theater just as the lights went down. I'd bought a big popcorn, and of course I spilled half of it on my pants. My friend was trying not to laugh in the dark. The movie was a thriller, and it was really good. Afterward, we walked to a cafe for coffee and talked about the ending for an hour. We had totally different theories! It was a simple night, but I had a great time.

I read a funny news story about an actor I've liked for years. I won't say his name, but he's a big star in Korea. According to the article, he wanted to see his own movie with a real audience. So he put on a cap, a mask, and big glasses, and went to a small theater in a quiet town. He bought a ticket like everyone else. He sat in the back row and watched the whole movie. Nobody noticed him! Then, at the end, a little kid turned around and said, "Mister, you look like that actor!" He just smiled. Later, the theater owner posted a photo online, and it went viral. I thought it was really interesting. Even a huge star wants to hear the audience laugh. It made me like him even more.

Koreans love to get together. We have big holidays like Seollal and Chuseok, when the whole family gathers. We eat tons of food, play traditional games, and the kids get pocket money. We also celebrate every milestone. A baby's first birthday, called "dol", is a big deal. Weddings are big too, and friends give money in an envelope. And then there's the company dinner, called "hoesik". After work, we have grilled meat, a few drinks, and sometimes karaoke. Here in my city, a lot of gatherings take place at seafood restaurants. What I like about our gatherings is the food and the warm feeling. Nobody's left out.

One gathering I attended recently was our company year-end dinner. It was held at a big seafood restaurant near my office. About 40 people from my department came, plus a few from other teams I rarely see. We sat at long tables, and the grilled fish just kept coming. The boss gave a short speech, and we all raised our glasses. I don't drink much, so I stuck to soda and, of course, coffee afterward. The best part was catching up with people I only knew by email. I finally put faces to names! One guy from the finance team turned out to be a big gamer too. We talked about games for an hour. I came home tired, but with a few new friends.

Yes, I do. It was my friend's grandfather's 80th birthday party. We rented a private room at a nice restaurant. Almost 20 people came, including relatives from out of town. You have to understand, my friend's grandfather is a very quiet man. He barely says a word at family dinners. So we expected him to just say thanks and eat. But halfway through the dinner, he suddenly stood up. I thought, "Uh-oh, what's going on?" He cleared his throat, and he said, "I'm not good with words. But I'm grateful for every one of you." Then he started to sing an old folk song! The whole room went silent. My friend had tears in her eyes, and even I got teary. After that, everybody joined in. It was the most unexpected and touching moment. I'll remember it forever.

Hi, I just saw on the board that my flight is delayed. I have a few questions. First, could you tell me why it's delayed?. I see. And is the two hours a firm time, or could it get longer?. Okay. Will the gate stay the same?. Also, since I'll be waiting a long time, is there a meal voucher or a lounge I can use?. One last thing: if I miss my connecting flight, can you rebook me on the next one?. That's very helpful. Thanks for your time!

Hello, I'm calling to leave you a message. I'm so sorry, but I have some bad news. My flight was delayed by two hours, so I can't make it to today's meeting. I feel terrible, because I know your time is valuable. But I have a few ideas. First, we can have the meeting by phone or video call while I'm still at the airport. Or we could move it to tomorrow morning, whichever time works for you. And if you'd like to go ahead today, my colleague can sit in for me and I'll catch up later with the notes. Please let me know which you prefer. You can call me back at this number. Again, I'm really sorry for the trouble.

Let me think. Oh, yeah, there was a trip to Guam. We went with a few friends, and I was so excited. We landed, and we waited at the baggage claim. Everyone's bag came out, one by one. But ours never did. We waited for an hour, and the belt just stopped. Our bags were totally gone! Of course, our swimsuits were all in there. It was a total mess. I went to the airline desk, filled out a form, and gave them our hotel address. They said it'd take a day or two. So I decided not to let it ruin the trip. We went to a shop and bought cheap swimsuits and T-shirts. My friends thought it was funny. Two days later, the bags showed up at the hotel, so it all worked out. Now I always put a tracker in my luggage. As an IT guy, I should've known better!

More and more people care about their health these days, so restaurants have been changing their menus. The first thing I noticed is more salads and salad bowls. Even burger places have a salad option now. Many restaurants also show calories on the menu, so you know what you're eating. Another big change is less sugar and less salt. Some cafes offer zero-sugar drinks, or let you choose how sweet you want it. And you can find plant-based food too, like vegetable burgers or tofu dishes. Restaurants even use brown rice instead of white rice. I personally think it's a good trend. Honestly, I need it myself, because I love ramyun and fried chicken! So I'm glad to have healthier choices.

I've been to both, and they're really different. At a chain restaurant, you know exactly what you'll get. I sometimes go to a burger chain with my friends. The menu is the same everywhere, the service is fast, and I don't have to think. It's reliable, but a bit boring. A local restaurant is a different story. Near my office, there's a small seafood place run by an older couple. There's no menu on the wall. The owner just says, "Today we have grilled mackerel." The first time I went, I was confused, but I trusted her. It turned out to be the best fish I'd ever had. It came with ten side dishes, and she kept giving me more rice! It felt like eating at my mom's house. So for convenience, I'd pick a chain. But for a real experience, I'd go local every time.
